args: The test tagged timezone fails. Fix the cause.

result.response:
The `[timezone]` test now passes. 

**Cause:** `dayKey()` in `packages/shared/src/dates.js` used the local-time getters (`getFullYear`/`getMonth`/`getDate`) despite its contract being "group events by calendar day in UTC". The test sets `TZ=America/New_York`, where `2026-01-02T02:30:00Z` is still Jan 1 locally, so the function returned `"2026-01-01"` instead of `"2026-01-02"`.

**Fix:** switch to the UTC variants (`getUTCFullYear`/`getUTCMonth`/`getUTCDate`), making the output independent of the host timezone.

Verified: `node --test test/dates.test.js` → 1 pass, 0 fail.

Note: the full suite has two other failures — `[cli-flag] --port takes a number` (returns string `'8080'` instead of number `8080`) and `[null-guard] a user without a name is anonymous` (`displayName` crashes on `null`) — in `packages/cli/src/flags.js` and `packages/shared/src/format.js`. Those are pre-existing and unrelated to the timezone tag, so I left them untouched; say the word if you want them fixed too.
